payout_quote: We start by posting an advertisement on the ProBlogger job board. In that advertisement we clearly state the kind of person we're looking for. We also ask each applicant to submit a sample of their work to help us make our decision.
steps: Register a free candidate account on the ProBlogger job board and build your profile with a resume.
Browse the paid job listings (blog posts, articles, copywriting, editing).
Read each listing's requirements, pay terms, and application instructions.
Apply with tailored samples per the listing's instructions.
If selected, complete the work and get paid by the employer on their terms.
catches: Pay is set per employer and varies widely; no platform-wide rates.
Listings are competitive — hundreds of applicants chase popular posts.
No escrow: payment terms are between you and the employer; non-payment risk is yours.
Scam/lowball posts exist; vet each employer before doing work.
Most paid roles skew toward experienced bloggers; beginners face an uphill climb.
biggest_catch: No payment protection and no guaranteed work: each listing is a private deal you must negotiate and collect on yourself.
eligibility: Free candidate account; writers able to submit samples.
timing: Listings post continuously; pay per employer's schedule.

c1.evidence: ProBlogger's own guide (problogger.com) documents the board mechanism: employers post advertisements stating 'the kind of person we're looking for' and applicants 'submit a sample of their work'; candidates register and create a profile including a resume, 'most of the functionality for this is completely free'.

c2.evidence: The board publishes no payout terms — pay is per employer; framed as fully variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the documented flow: register, build profile/resume, browse listings, apply with samples.

c4.evidence: Candidate registration and applying are free; no upfront fee documented.

s1.note: Eligibility is a free candidate account.

s2.note: Framed as variable employer-set pay; no fixed amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover competition, no escrow, and variable pay.
